$comment: Corpus for bet B1 (docs/bets.md) and the author's rulings on pairs check:corpus flags. Each distinct entry says why two similar mechanisms are different ideas; delete an entry to reopen it. Rulings of 2026-10-07 were made under the author's instruction to combine mechanisms that are the same idea and keep the rest; coercive-waiting was combined into delay-as-force that day. On 2026-10-07 the author asked for a decision on the three books' central mechanisms: running-hot/human-heat-sink was combined into crumple-zone (same lever and evidence), and transfer-success was kept distinct. On 2026-10-08 the author asked for the remaining open pair to be decided: crumple-zone/coercion-by-design was combined into refusability-gap (same lever and evidence). Each merge is kept under "merged" with both mechanisms as they were before it, so check:corpus --eval can score embedding models against the author's rulings.

distinct.reason: Both are procedure doing moral work, aimed in opposite directions. Bureaucracy as moral technology is the institution's cover: harm counts as acceptable because the process was followed. Clearance culture is a gate on the person: after any deviation, they must win permission to re-enter. Cover for the institution versus a re-entry burden on the individual.
Reversibility gap is the system's asymmetry: it harms fast and restores slowly. Reversal capacity is who can afford to contest at all. Undo speed versus the resources to use recourse.
Caricature is an institution enforcing a distorted version of its own principles. Vibe legitimacy is authority claimed through aesthetic and affect instead of competence.
Delay as force uses waiting as leverage to win a concession or a withdrawal. Temporal capture is people's time taken as an uncounted resource, even when no decision is being forced.
Discretion as gate is a decider's unbounded latitude over cases, fixed with reason codes and calibration. Credibility as access control is whose word counts: standing, not procedure.
Reputation membrane protects an institution's image with ethics language. Credibility as access control decides which people are believed.
Refusability is the ability to say no before harm. Reversibility is undoing harm after it lands.
Death of slack is one cause: buffers removed for efficiency. Crumple zone is the broader result, people absorbing systemic failure, which other transfers also produce.
Discretion as gate is opaque latitude over who gets access. Reputation membrane is image management after harm.
Pyrrhic condition is winning in a way that destroys the prize. Cowardice of inference is reaching the right conclusion and not acting on it.
Attrition by queue removes people through structure (resets, expiries, handoffs) whatever the elapsed time. Delay as force is duration itself used as pressure.
Compliance trap secures compliance through warmth, so refusal feels cruel. Bureaucracy as moral technology uses procedure so harm feels acceptable.
Compliance trap works on the person asked to comply. Vibe legitimacy is how an authority claims standing.
Caricature enforces distorted principles. Sanctiphagy extracts and brands moral goodness itself.

Transfer success is about authority: decision rights stay up while blame and cost move down; you test it by comparing who decided with who pays. Crumple zone is about missing buffers: shocks land on people because slack and rollback were never built; you test it by asking whether backup would have spared them.

merged.reason: Same lever and same evidence: waiting used as leverage until the person with less buffer gives up or accepts worse terms, tested by asking what changes when a firm deadline or interim protection exists.

before.title: Coercive Waiting
before.definition: Time is used as pressure: delays exhaust options, narrow choices, and coerce agreement.
is: A pattern where waiting increases the cost of refusal.
A tactic that relies on fatigue, deadlines, or uncertainty to force consent.

before.title: Delay as force
before.definition: A governance pattern where elapsed time is weaponized to reduce claims, lower payouts, or induce withdrawal without explicit denial.
is: Wait times and review loops that increase burden for the claimant while preserving institutional flexibility.
Time costs shifted onto people with urgent needs, unstable income, or fragile health.

merged.reason: Same idea under the same test: institutions stay stable by routing shocks into people instead of building buffers, checked by asking who absorbs the load when there is no backup.

before.title: Human heat sink
before.definition: A system-stability pattern where institutions preserve output by exporting volatility into people's unpaid labor, delay exposure, and physiological stress.
is: The organization remains operational by routing spikes into waiting, paperwork, escalation friction, and emotional regulation demands on individuals.
Cooling capacity (buffers, slack, rollback, coverage) is underbuilt while throughput targets remain unchanged.

before.title: Crumple Zone
before.definition: Individuals absorb the force of systemic failures. Human bodies become the cheapest shock absorbers.
is: Systems transfer risk to individuals rather than containing it
Institutional stability is purchased by externalizing pressure onto people
The human body is treated as the cheapest available infrastructure

merged.reason: Same lever and same evidence: refusal left out of a system's design makes participation involuntary, checked by asking where you cannot say no and what an optional version would look like. Refusability gap names the lever; coercion by design was the claim that the lever is a design choice.

before.title: Refusability Gap
before.definition: The ability to say no is treated as optional when it should be a structural design requirement.
is: Refusal is not currently designed into most systems
The absence of refusal points is a political choice
Systems that make refusal impossible are coercive by design

before.title: Coercion by Design
before.definition: Coercion is not accidental. It is designed into systems, and therefore can be designed out.
is: Coercive outcomes result from design choices
Systems can be built where coercion is structurally impossible
Designers should bear the burden of proving non-coercion
